_meta.purpose: Smoke woods. Eight woods, matching the coverage of the approved Smoke Wood Pairing master. Flavour character and pairings are barbecue convention: FSIS names hickory, apple and maple as giving the most satisfactory smoke flavour, and Texas A&M names hickory, oak, pecan and mesquite as the four primary Texas woods; beyond that no authoritative body ranks smoke strength. Records are labelled accordingly. Woods have no safety dimension EXCEPT the FSIS rule to use only wood intended for cooking, never treated or painted wood, and never galvanized or makeshift containers.
_meta.record_shape: slug, name, strength (mild | medium | strong), flavor_character, best_animals[], best_cuts[], blend_ideas[], avoid_or_use_lightly_with[], regional_note, source_refs, review_status, updated_at
_meta.safety_note: Cook only with wood sold or known to be safe for smoking: no pressure-treated, painted, stained or glued wood, no softwood construction scrap. FSIS: buy commercial charcoal briquettes or aromatic wood chips.

woods.name: Oak
woods.flavor_character: Balanced, clean, dependable. The all-purpose smoke and the Central Texas standard (post oak).
blend_ideas: oak + cherry for beef colour and balance
woods.regional_note: One of Texas A&M's four primary Texas barbecue woods; red oak is the Santa Maria tri-tip tradition.

woods.name: Hickory
woods.flavor_character: Bold, savoury, bacon-like. The classic pork and rib smoke; heavy-handed on poultry.
woods.regional_note: FSIS names hickory among the woods giving the most satisfactory flavour; Texas A&M lists it among the four primary Texas woods.

woods.name: Mesquite
woods.flavor_character: Intense, earthy, fast-burning. Best for hot-and-fast beef; turns harsh over a long cook.
blend_ideas: mesquite + oak to tame it for brisket
woods.regional_note: One of Texas A&M's four primary Texas woods; South and West Texas tradition.

woods.name: Pecan
woods.flavor_character: Nutty, warm, slightly sweet. A softer relative of hickory.
woods.regional_note: One of Texas A&M's four primary Texas woods.

woods.name: Apple
woods.flavor_character: Sweet, fruity, gentle. Builds slowly; forgiving on poultry and pork.
avoid_or_use_lightly_with: heavy beef cuts where it disappears
woods.regional_note: FSIS names apple among the woods giving the most satisfactory smoke flavour.

woods.name: Cherry
woods.flavor_character: Fruity, mild, and it colours the meat a deep mahogany. Pairs with almost everything.
woods.regional_note: Widely used for colour on competition ribs and chicken.

woods.name: Maple
woods.flavor_character: Soft, sweet, subtle. Good with pork, poultry, ham and vegetables.
woods.regional_note: FSIS names maple among the woods giving the most satisfactory smoke flavour.

woods.name: Alder
woods.flavor_character: Delicate, clean, faintly sweet. The Pacific Northwest salmon wood.
blend_ideas: alder + apple for a gentle salmon blend
avoid_or_use_lightly_with: heavy beef; it is too light to register
woods.regional_note: Traditional Pacific Northwest wood for salmon.
